title: Regime-Closure Epistemology (RCE): A General Principle of Cross-Domain Validation in Coupled Multi-Scale Systems
description: Introduces Regime-Closure Epistemology (RCE) as an operational principle for validating coupled multi-scale systems. The paper specifies five joint conditions—regime locality, variety closure, modelling closure, frozen-parameter governance, and external arbitration via sealed predictions—arguing that validation is sound if and only if these hold. It consolidates EFC machinery (EBE, RCMP, L0–L3 architecture, sealed predictions, and a live falsification ledger) and deposits pre-registered cross-domain predictions.

coupled_subsystems_condition.description: RCE applies to systems with at least two coupled subsystems operating at scale-separated timescales.

rce_validity_iff.description: Validation (V) is sound if and only if the five RCE conditions hold jointly: C1 regime locality; C2 variety closure (Ashby); C3 modelling closure (Conant–Ashby); C4 frozen-parameter governance; C5 external arbitration via sealed predictions (Beer).

key_results.main_finding: States and operationalizes RCE: validation in coupled multi-scale systems is valid iff five specified regime-closure conditions are jointly satisfied, with sealed, pre-registered cross-domain predictions deposited for external arbitration.

sealed_predictions.statement: Seven pre-registered cross-domain predictions with explicit thresholds and named arbiters are sealed and deposited against this paper’s DOI; details and hashes are provided in the associated validation ledger.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: External arbitration of the sealed prediction set as deposited (hash-verified) under this DOI; failure to meet the pre-registered thresholds constitutes falsification.

kill_criteria: KC1: Necessity counterexample — Demonstrate a coupled multi-scale system (N ≥ 2) where a validation procedure is externally adjudicated as valid despite at least one of the five RCE conditions not holding.

KC2: Sufficiency counterexample — Implement and verify all five RCE conditions in a coupled multi-scale system and show that the sealed, pre-registered predictions fail their explicit thresholds under external arbitration.

KC3: No ‘dark X’ symptom under condition failure — Identify a domain that applies single-regime methodology to a clearly coupled multi-regime system without generating residual categories or mystery entities required to close quantitative/causal ledgers.

KC4: Persistence of mystery entities after regime-consistent re-architecture — After installing regime-consistent measurement and frozen-parameter governance, show that the prior residual (‘dark X’/idiopathic/exogenous) does not resolve into couplings/buffering/scale-transition operators.

KC5: Operational instantiation failure — Show that the claimed operational machinery (sealed numerical predictions with deposit hashes and a living falsification ledger) is not present or cannot be verified for this paper’s deposits and associated EFC apparatus.

related_packages.role: Regime-locked measurement as a general structural constraint
